articles.headline: NFL chief medical officer: Eagles' approach to Hurts was 'appropriately guarded'
articles.description: At the owners meetings Tuesday in New York, NFL officials staunchly defended the process involving Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts and his blood clot issue, with chief medical officer Allen Sills addressing reporters in a media availability.
articles.body:
NEW YORK -- NFL officials Tuesday staunchly defended the medical process involving Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts' blood clot issue.

NFL chief medical officer Allen Sills was blunt in a news conference from the owners meetings.

"The notion that there's external factors that any of our physicians would put a player in harm's way -- that's nonsense," Sills said.

The NFL is not punishing the Eagles for the handling of Hurts, who was cleared to play before Week 5 against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London's Tottenham Hotspur Stadium after he was initially diagnosed with a superficial blood clot in his calf.

Hurts, 28, is expected to miss the rest of the season after doctors discovered multiple blood clots in the quarterback's lungs days after the game.  Hurts will undergo treatment involving blood thinners that is expected to sideline the three-time Pro Bowler for around three months.

Hurts' agent, Nicole Lynn, and the Eagles released a statement Monday detailing Hurts' condition. Lynn and the Eagles said Hurts has deep vein thrombosis and bilateral pulmonary emboli, meaning a blood clot traveled from his legs to his lungs.

NFL officials confirmed Tuesday that it had been in contact with Eagles medical personnel and Cleveland Clinic London throughout the process of Hurts being treated. Sills called the Eagles' treatment of Hurts "very conservative, very patient-focused and appropriately guarded in every step."

This week's news prompted rampant speculation about why the Eagles allowed Hurts to play in London.

Jeff Miller, NFL executive vice president overseeing player health and safety, called such speculation "considerable and uninformed," as well as "unfounded."

"Conservative steps were taken to ensure Jalen Hurts' health was always made the first priority and continues to be," Miller said.

The NFL declined to discuss specifics of Hurts' case, citing medical privacy. But Sills, who has been a team physical for three decades, said he has "tremendous confidence" in the Eagles' medical staff. The NFL works one to two years in advance of international games to prep for medical care, identifying local hospitals, physicians and resources at every site.

The medical experts tasked with evaluating players in such cases are not influenced by the team, Sills said.

"There is no doctor who is taking orders from a football person, a non-medical person. Period," Sills said.

Doctors speculating online about "what should have been done" without all the data or being in the room with a patient are "unprofessional and unethical" in doing so, Sills said, citing a "sacred trust" between physicians and patients.

The NFL has tracked blood clot cases every season for the last decade and shares the data with the NFLPA, Sills said. Each year features a handful of cases.

"This isn't really a new situation, but it's something we examine," Sills said.

articles.headline: Paul George's 38-point debut not enough as Piston rally late to down Celtics
articles.description: Paul George scored 38 points -- the most by a Celtic in his debut, and the fifth-most by a player in his first game with an NBA franchise -- in a 121-113 collapsing defeat to the Pistons on Tuesday. But as George put it: "I'm not a moral victory guy."
articles.body:
DETROIT -- Paul George looks like he's still got it.

He scored 38 points -- the most by a Boston Celtic in his debut, and the fifth-most by a player in his first game with an NBA franchise -- in a 121-113 collapsing defeat to the Detroit Pistons on Tuesday.

"I'm not a moral victory guy," George said after making 12 of 21 shots, including 7 of 12 3-pointers. "It means nothing."

Maybe not, but the nine-time All-Star was impressive and earned a spot in rarified air,

The NBA scoring record for a debut was set by Kyrie Irving in 2019, when he had 50 with the Brooklyn Nets.

Kiki Vandeweghe had 47 points in his first game with Portland in 1984, Wilt Chamberlain scored 43 points in his NBA debut with Philadelphia in 1959 and Damian Lillard had 39 points in his Milwaukee debut in 2023.

George, in his 17th season, was acquired in a trade with the 76ers last summer in exchange for 2024 NBA Finals MVP Jaylen Brown.

Even though George wasn't celebrating his performance due to the loss, the 36-year-old forward was encouraged by his health.

Injuries -- and a 25-game suspension for flunking a drug test -- limited him to 37 and 41 games the last two regular seasons with the Sixers.

During training camp with the Celtics, George said his legs felt heavy and winded.

In Game 1 with his fifth team, he didn't know what to respect.

"It's hard to know until the lights come on," George said. "It was a rough camp for me."

He looked smooth in Motown in 31 minutes with five steals, five rebounds and three assists.

"It was a thing to watch," teammate Derrick White said. "He got hot and we tried to find him."

The Celtics found George early in the third quarter, leading to him making three 3-pointers in less than a minute to put them ahead 72-50.

Boston then became the fifth team in 30 seasons to lose a season-opening game after leading by 22 points allowed Detroit to earn the biggest comeback win in a league opener since 1997.

"If we're in the driver's seat like that, we'll learn how to close out games," George said.

George certainly did his part.

"He was unbelievable," Jayson Tatum said.

Tatum, meanwhile, was off his game.

The six-time All-Star missed 17 of 23 shots had 13 points and 11 assists. His lack of hustle on defense allowed Javonte Green to take his time for a fifth 3-pointer that gave the Pistons a 13-point lead with 3:33 left that capped a 23-0 run.

George, though, gave the Celtics a lot to like.

"Just his comfort level," reigning NBA Coach of the Year Joe Mazzulla said. "The game found him, he made some great reads throughout the game. It was good. He was able to find advantages for himself and others, we just have to continue that.

articles.headline: NBA opening day: Live updates, highlights from tripleheader
articles.description: The 2026-27 NBA season is back with a bang. Follow along for all of the live updates and highlights from the tripleheader.
articles.headlineJa: NBA開幕日：3試合同時開催のライブ速報とハイライト
articles.descriptionJa: 2026-27 NBAシーズンが華々しく開幕。3試合同時開催のライブ速報とハイライトを随時お届けします。
articles.body:
The NBA is back with a bang.

The 2026-27 season tips off with a tripleheader, beginning with a rare daytime game between the Detroit Pistons and Boston Celtics. That sets up ring night at Madison Square Garden as the New York Knicks host the Philadelphia 76ers. The night concludes with a rematch of the 2026 Western Conference finals between the San Antonio Spurs and Oklahoma City Thunder.

Each game bring its own headlines, starting off in Detroit. The Pistons are coming off a 60-win season, while the Celtics debut the duo of Jayson Tatum and Paul George.

The Knicks are raising a banner for the first time in 50 years. Who will look to spoil their night? None other than the new-look 76ers, with Jaylen Brown and LeBron James teaming up with Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey and VJ Edgecombe. 

Five months after defeating Oklahoma City in Game 7 to reach the Finals, San Antonio welcomes its Western Conference rivals in another battle. The Thunder and Spurs return most of their cores, setting up a matchup full of familiar matchups and tension.

We'll have all of the top moments and highlights from the NBA's tripleheader. Follow along below.

articles.headline: Football watchdog chair asserts 'absolute' power to force City sale
articles.description: The Independent Football Regulator will have "absolute power" to force Manchester City's owners to sell if they are ultimately found to have run the club improperly, the watchdog's chair has said.
articles.body:
The Independent Football Regulator will have "absolute power" to force Manchester City's owners to sell if they are ultimately found to have run the club improperly, the watchdog's chair has said.

City have been found guilty of circumventing Premier League rules by an independent commission, which found they set up "sham" commercial arrangements to inflate revenues or reduce costs by over £900 million ($1.2 billion) over a nine-season period.

They were also found to have made "concerted efforts" to "stop and frustrate" the Premier League's investigation into those arrangements.

David Kogan, the chair of the IFR, told "The Rest Is Football" podcast it was premature to talk about any action his organisation might take, with City having lodged an appeal against the original commission's verdict.

However, he confirmed the IFR had the power to force a sale by the club's owner Sheikh Mansour if that was felt to be appropriate.

"We have the power to ask an owner to step away from a club if we believe that they run a club in a way that is neither fit, fair or done with propriety," Kogan said.

Asked if an owner could refuse to divest, Kogan replied: "No, no, no. We've got absolute power to do so."

On the possibility of the IFR investigating City, Kogan said: "I am not going to get pushed into making any judgement on this until we've seen all of those questions being answered and then we will have to decide whether we're going to mount our own investigation and come to a conclusion on that and what we're going to do. And pre-empting that would be a colossal mistake."

Kogan has already pledged to resign if there is any political interference in any investigation the IFR may undertake into City, amid concerns it could become a diplomatic issue between the United Kingdom and the United Arab Emirates.

articles.headline: NBA season tips off with Pistons rallying to beat Celtics 121-113, spoiling Paul George's debut
articles.description: — Javonte Green scored 19 points after not playing in the first half and Cade Cunningham finished with 22 points and eight assists, helping the Detroit Pistons come back and beat the
articles.body:
DETROIT -- — Javonte Green scored 19 points after not playing in the first half and Cade Cunningham finished with 22 points and eight assists, helping the Detroit Pistons come back and beat the Boston Celtics 121-113 on Tuesday.


              The NBA picked the matinee matchup to tip off the season and it delivered plenty of entertainment.


              Paul George scored 38 points, the most by a Celtic in his debut. The nine-time All-Star, in his 17th season, showed he's still got it in his first game with Boston since it acquired him from Philadelphia in exchange for 2024 NBA Finals MVP Jaylen Brown.


              Jayson Tatum, though, was off his game.


              He missed 17 of 23 shots had 13 points and 11 assists. His lack of hustle on defense allowed Green to take his time for a fifth 3-pointer that gave the Pistons a 13-point lead with 3:33 left.


              Tatum, a six-time All-Star, is set to play his first full season since tearing his Achilles tendon in May 2025.


              Boston took its biggest lead early in the third quarter at 72-50 after George made three 3-pointers in less than a minute.


              Detroit cut its deficit to six points after three quarters and surged ahead in the fourth. Green made a go-ahead 3, Duren added a three-point play and Robinson connected on a 3 to put the Pistons ahead 107-99 with 5:10 to go.


              Jalen Duren had 22 points and nine rebounds, Duncan Robinson scored 21 points — making 5 of 9 3-pointers — and Ausar Thompson added 11 points and 11 rebounds for the Pistons.


              Boston's Derrick White and Payton Pritchard scored 17 points apiece.


              Up next
              Celtics: Host the New York Knicks on Friday.


              Pistons: At Miami on Friday.

articles.headline: Sources: Barcelona report PSG to UEFA for 'aggressive' tifo
articles.description: Barcelona have reported Paris Saint-Germain to UEFA for the tifo unfurled by the French club's supporters before Tuesday's Champions League game, a source told ESPN.
articles.body:
Barcelona have reported Paris Saint-Germain to UEFA for the tifo unfurled by the French club's supporters before Tuesday's Champions League game, a source told ESPN.

As the players came on to the pitch before kickoff, fans behind one of the goals at Parc des Princes held up a giant banner which showed a masked figure carrying a chainsaw and destroying the Barça badge.

Underneath were the words: "Massacre, Parisian style."

In addition, pyrotechnics were used to mimic the sparks coming from the chainsaw as it hacked away at the Barça crest.

The source said the imagery evoked was both "overly aggressive and offensive."

On the pitch, PSG ran out 4-2 winners in an entertaining game between two of Europe's most in-form sides.

Desiré Douré, Lucas Hernández, Vitinha and Fabián Ruiz were all on target as PSG made it three wins out of three in the Champions League this season.

For Barça, who twice levelled through Xavi Espart and Lamine Yamal, it represented their first loss of the season, bringing an end to their 11-game winning streak.

Both teams have big games to come in their respective leagues this weekend.

PSG face Lyon in a top-of-the-table clash in Ligue 1, while Barça host rivals Real Madrid in the Clásico.

articles.headline: Ngumoha sparks Liverpool's comeback Champions League win
articles.description: Still just 18, Rio Ngumoha produced the finest game of his Liverpool career thus far in helping the Reds overturn a two-goal deficit vs. Villarreal.
articles.body:
LIVERPOOL, England -- Rio Ngumoha's reputation must have preceded him. Liverpool's UEFA Champions League clash with Villarreal was only a few minutes old, and already the opposition defenders had begun to double-team the young forward in an attempt to stop him wreaking havoc down the right flank.

Their efforts proved futile; Ngumoha provided two outstanding assists to help Liverpool come from 2-0 down to claim a 4-3 victory at Anfield. The England international did not manage to get on the scoresheet, but he produced what was undeniably the most accomplished display of his fledgling senior career, providing Andoni Iraola's side with the impetus required to overcome its sluggish start and secure a third straight win in all competitions.

"It's up there with one of the best I've played," Ngumoha told Amazon Prime postmatch. "I enjoyed myself and the team helped me a lot. Whenever I get the ball and there's an opportunity to go one v. one or two v. one, I believe in myself. I'll just keep going and be ruthless."

Ngumoha came into this season with a point to prove. Having broken into Liverpool's first team as a left winger under Arne Slot last term, the forward has found his route to regular game time in his favored position stymied by the summer arrival of the £123 million Bradley Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain.

The further addition of Víctor Muñoz from Osasuna, plus the renaissance of Cody Gakpo, has only served to intensify competition in attack. It is the kind of challenge that some young players might have shied away from, but on the evidence of his most recent display, it has spurred Ngumoha on to new heights.

"Any position -- right wing, left wing -- I just try my best especially on the ball just to beat my man as best as I can," Ngumoha told ESPN during preseason. "The more I keep learning in training and games, I'll definitely improve. To be adaptable is a skill that I need, definitely."

That versatility has paid dividends for Ngumoha over the past few weeks. The 18-year-old started on the right against LASK Linz last week before impressing in the same position in his cameo against Brentford at the weekend.

Tuesday night, though, was a coming of age. Ngumoha became the youngest player on record (since 2008-09) to complete five-plus dribbles (7), have 10-plus touches in the opposition box (12) and register an assist (2) in a Champions League match.

His relentlessness and ability to torment defenders showed that, while Liverpool might not have signed a like-for-like replacement for the talismanic Mohamed Salah, they still have a potent attacking threat on the right-hand side.

Certainly, Ngumoha's flair and dynamism was needed against Villarreal given how poorly Liverpool had started the game. The Reds found themselves a goal down inside four minutes after a lapse from Virgil van Dijk opened the door for Villarreal's Georges Mikautadze to slot home past Alisson.

articles.headline: Knicks reverse course, hang banner for NBA Cup title
articles.description: The Knicks on Tuesday hung a banner at Madison Square Garden to celebrate the NBA Cup title they won last season.
articles.body:
NEW YORK -- The Knicks are having a banner night -- two of them -- Tuesday.

Before raising their championship banner ahead of their season opener against the Philadelphia 76ers, the NBA champions hung one at Madison Square Garden to celebrate the NBA Cup title they won last season.

The Knicks broke with tradition last December when they became the first team to win the in-season tournament and then not commemorate it with a banner. They said at the time they were looking ahead to bigger things.

They ended up getting the biggest thing possible by beating the San Antonio Spurs in the NBA Finals for their first championship since 1973.

The Knicks also defeated the Spurs in the NBA Cup final. The NBA Cup banner went up sometime after the Sixers held their morning shootaround at the arena.

"I haven't seen it, but I think it's just a recognition of what our journey was like last year, you know?" coach Mike Brown said. "There were a lot of, obviously, ups and downs throughout the course of the year, and our guys rallied and figured out a way to win the NBA Cup, and then you go ahead and win the regular-season final, or excuse me, the end-of-season final, and it's just a recognition to not just to our guys, but to the fans out there."

The NBA Cup banner was the first hung at Madison Square Garden by the Knicks since they won the Atlantic Division title in 2012-13.

articles.headline: Tired Barcelona undone by 'too many mistakes' as perfect start ends at PSG
articles.description: Barcelona coach Hansi Flick says his tired Barcelona side made too many mistakes as their perfect start to the season ended with a 4-2 defeat to Paris Saint-Germain on Wednesday in the Champions League.
articles.body:
PARIS -- Barcelona coach Hansi Flick said his tired side made too many mistakes as their perfect start to the season ended with a 4-2 defeat to Paris Saint-Germain on Wednesday in the Champions League.

Desiré Doué, Lucas Hernández, Vitinha and Fabián Ruiz were all on target as PSG edged an enthralling game at the Parc des Princes to make it three wins from three in Europe this season.

Xavi Espart and Lamine Yamal had twice drawn Barça level before the Spanish champions conceded twice late on as their 11-game winning run at the start of the new campaign came to an end.

- PSG injuries can't overshadow signature UCL win over Barcelona

- Barcelona, PSG thriller in Champions League proves these are the two best

"I think it was a fantastic game from both teams," Flick said in the post-game news conference. "We made too many mistakes, especially in ball possession, easy ball losses.

"This is what we have to analyse. But I saw a lot of good things also. For me it was a great test for us. You saw today in which areas we have to improve. This is what we will do.

"We have to understand the mistakes happen because [the players] are not fresh. What they had to do the last couple of weeks is unbelievable. I appreciate the attitude. A lot of things were fantastic."

The fixture had been billed as a clash between the best two sides in the world right now: back-to-back European champions PSG taking on a Barça side that had scored 48 goals in their 11 wins this season.

Barcelona's 11-game winning start to the season in all competitions had been tied for the third-longest winning start by a team from Europe's top five leagues and tied for the longest by a Spanish club.

However, Flick lamented Barça's preparation for the match, with their flight back from Seville after beating Real Betis on Saturday cancelled due to storms in Spain.

"Everyone knows what happens after [the Betis win], so it's not the perfect recovery," he added. "It's not an excuse, just for you to understand why maybe we were not at the top level.

"But it was a good level. We have to learn from this game. PSG had a lot of chances -- Joan García was fantastic in goal for us -- but so did we. We have to take them. This is what I saw from PSG today.

"But in October you can't win titles. You win the Champions League in June. This is the way how we want to do it."

Flick also confirmed the surprise decision to start Rodri on the bench was made with Sunday's visit from Real Madrid LaLiga in mind.

Victory in the Clásico at Spotify Camp Nou would move Barça nine points clear of José Mourinho's side and extend their winning streak in the league to 10 games.

"Yes," Flick said when asked if Rodri, who came on for the final 30 minutes, was reserved for Madrid. "He played a lot of minutes with [Spain] and also the last games with us after the break.

"I spoke with him and told him we make this decision and [Marc] Bernal started. For me, it was a good solution. Hopefully he's fresh on Sunday."

Dani

articles.headline: Steelers bring back veteran Marquez Valdes-Scantling amid receiver injury woes
articles.description: The Steelers, in need of help at wide receiver with Michael Pittman Jr. and Roman Wilson out because of injuries, signed veteran Marquez Valdes-Scantling on Tuesday.
articles.body:
PITTSBURGH -- Marquez Valdes-Scantling is back with the Pittsburgh Steelers.

The Steelers signed the veteran wide receiver to their practice squad Tuesday ahead of a trip to Paris to take on the New Orleans Saints.

Valdes-Scantling, 32, spent a portion of the 2025 season in Pittsburgh, catching 10 passes for 80 yards and a touchdown in five games before adding three receptions in a first-round playoff loss to the Houston Texans.

Pittsburgh is in need of help at wide receiver after Michael Pittman Jr. and Roman Wilson were both put on injured reserve in the past week, leaving little experienced depth behind DK Metcalf and rookie Germie Bernard, who combined for 22 catches in a comeback win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday.

The Steelers are Valdes-Scantling's third team in less than two months. He was released by the Dallas Cowboys in late August then signed with the Los Angeles Chargers in September, catching two passes for 22 yards in three games before being released last week.

Valdes-Scantling has a history with Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers going back to their time together with the Green Bay Packers. Valdes-Scantling had 123 receptions in four seasons with the Packers from 2018 to 2021.

articles.headline: JJ Redick says Lakers' 'biggest unknown' is how they will deal with adversity
articles.description: JJ Redick said the Lakers' "biggest unknown" is how his new-look roster sans LeBron James will deal with adversity.
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES -- As the Los Angeles Lakers finish their final preparations for the first game of the post-LeBron James era, coach JJ Redick said Tuesday that his "biggest unknown" is how his new-look roster will "deal with adversity."

"That's different for every team," Redick said. "That's different, maybe, in how we deal with adversity in November versus how we deal with adversity in March. Hopefully, there's growth throughout the season so we can deal with adversity in the right way, and that will ultimately prepare us for a deep playoff run."

Though Redick predicted that the Lakers will prove to be "really committed to each other," he acknowledged that his large-market team faces an outsized amount of intense scrutiny whenever it struggles.

"It could be [Wednesday] night, you're going to come to me and tell me that the world is ending and the sky is falling," Redick said. "We've got to work through that together. [The scrutiny] depends on the team and depends on the market. With the Lakers, how many times did we lose last year? Twenty-nine times? [So, the sky was falling] 29 times."

Luka Doncic and the Lakers will open the season Wednesday hosting Stephen Curry and the Golden State Warriors at Crypto.com Arena. The Lakers enter the season without James, who spent the past eight seasons as the face of the franchise. Additionally, Rui Hachimura, Marcus Smart, Deandre Ayton, Luke Kennard, Jaxson Hayes, Gabe Vincent, Dalton Knecht and Maxi Kleber all departed from last season's roster.

During a transformative summer, the Lakers acquired starting center Walker Kessler in a sign-and-trade with the Utah Jazz, drafted Cameron Carr in the first round, and added Quentin Grimes, Sandro Mamukelashvili, Collin Sexton, Ziaire Williams, Matisse Thybulle and Kevon Looney in free agency.

As a result of that extensive overhaul around stars Doncic and Austin Reaves, NBA general managers dubbed the Lakers as one of the league's "toughest to predict" teams in an annual survey. Redick dismissed that label, saying that the survey was a "fun exercise" but that "predictions don't mean anything."

But the lingering unknowns about the Lakers include their opening night starting lineup. Doncic, Reaves and Kessler will start, but Redick has yet to announce who will join them at the two forward positions. Redick used 12 different players in his starting lineups during the preseason as the Lakers posted a 2-3 record.

Reaves, who is now the Lakers' longest-tenured player, says he believes this season's group is composed of "high-character guys" who will "come together when adversity hits instead of splitting apart."

"We're good enough to win a lot of games, but I don't think we're as good as we can be," Reaves said. "With the [repetitions] and in-game competition and going through adversity, that will only build us to be better in the long haul."

articles.headline: Commanders' Quinn, Daniels discuss QB's throwaway on fourth-down play
articles.description: Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels shouldn't have thrown a fourth-down pass away in the second quarter of Monday night's loss, coach Dan Quinn said.
articles.headlineJa: コマンダーズのクイン監督とダニエルズ、4ダウン目のスローアウェイについて語る
articles.descriptionJa: コマンダーズのダン・クイン監督は、月曜夜の敗戦における第2クォーター、QBジェイデン・ダニエルズが4ダウン目でパスをスローアウェイすべきではなかったと述べた。
articles.body:
Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels shouldn't have thrown a fourth-down pass away in the second quarter of Monday night's 23-17 loss to the San Francisco 49ers, coach Dan Quinn said.

On a fourth-and-2 from the 49ers' 13-yard line, Daniels dropped back to pass and left the pocket after the 49ers started to generate pressure.

As Daniels ran to his right, two defenders pursued him, including linebacker Fred Warner. A flag was also thrown in front of Daniels. He could not make the first down running and with no open receiver in front of him he threw the ball away.

Quinn said he spoke to Daniels about the play.

"Even when you know there's a penalty, you still take your shot, man, to go throw it, complete it," Quinn said. "You don't know if it's gonna get picked up."

As it turned out the penalty wasn't an offsides call on the defense, which would have given Washington a first down. Rather it was an illegal shift on the Commanders.

"I didn't know. It could have been offside, it could have been on us," Daniels said if he anticipated an offsides call.

San Francisco declined the penalty because of the incompletion.

Daniels did complete 29-of-40 passes for 300 yards and two touchdowns on Monday night. He helped Washington rally from a 20-3 halftime deficit and drove the Commanders deep into 49ers territory late in the game with a chance to take the lead.

"Like most things with him, there's some plays that you said, that's an incredible throw," Quinn said. "And there's other ones I'd love him to stay through the [read]."

He said he knew it would be tough for Daniels to gain yards scrambling because of the 49ers' team speed and their zone coverage with eyes on the quarterback. Indeed he rushed only four times for 10 yards.

Daniels was playing his second game wearing a brace on his left elbow that he dislocated in Week 2. Quinn said as Daniels evolves in coordinator David Blough's offense he'd like him to scramble more to throw. But he also knows he can make plays multiple ways.

"He always can make some throws that just kinda leaves you thinking, 'Man, there it is. There's only a few guys that can make that throw or that play,'" Quinn said.

articles.headline: Sources: Rams signing free agent kicker Brandon McManus
articles.description: The Rams, after releasing Harrison Mevis and an injury to Blake Grupe, are signing free agent kicker Brandon McManus, sources told NFL Network.
articles.headlineJa: 関係者発表：ラムズがフリーエージェントのキッカー、ブランドン・マクマナスと契約へ
articles.descriptionJa: NFL Networkが伝えた関係者の話によると、ラムズはハリソン・メビスの放出とブレイク・グルーペの負傷を受け、フリーエージェントのキッカーであるブランドン・マクマナスと契約する。
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES -- The Rams are signing kicker Brandon McManus, sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo on Tuesday.

The Rams worked out McManus and free agent kicker Matt Prater on Tuesday after kicker Blake Grupe tore his ACL in a Week 6 loss to the Arizona Cardinals.

Grupe was playing in his first game for the Rams after he was signed to replace Harrison Mevis, who missed a 50-yard field goal attempt and then had a 48-yarder blocked in overtime of the Rams' Week 5 loss.

McManus last kicked for the Green Bay Packers after signing with them in 2024. He was 44 of 51 for Green Bay over two seasons, with six misses coming during the 2025 season.

He spent his first nine seasons with the Denver Broncos and one with the Jacksonville Jaguars and was not on a roster to start the 2024 season while being investigated by the NFL for possible violations of the personal conduct policy. In September 2024, the NFL announced McManus was not in violation of the policy and he signed with the Packers three weeks later.
